reasons: Direction is correct: Commerce One is the licensor and Corio (our client) the licensee, so widening the grant's beneficiaries is a pro-Customer edit consistent with the rule.

The gap is real and correctly diagnosed: no Section 2 grant mentions affiliates or contractors, and 'affiliate' appears nowhere in the agreement, even though Section 14.8 contemplates subcontracting and Corio Servers may be 'operated by or for Corio' — leaving affiliates/subcontractors exercising licensed rights outside the grant.

The redline is the smallest edit that reaches the position: a new Section 2.11 appended after 2.10 extending all Section 2 licences to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, with Corio responsible for their compliance; original paragraph text (p0030, p0033, p0045) is left intact, so the high changed-character footprint is purely additive.
Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the written-notice affiliate fallback without lecturing.

Remaining rule elements are already satisfied in the contract as cited (2.1 perpetual/irrevocable/paid-up-style grant, 14.1 successor transfer, 11.2 termination only for uncured material breach), so no further edits were needed; the only minor residual is that 2.2 is 'fully paid up, perpetual' without the word 'irrevocable', which is substantively covered by the perpetual grant plus breach-only termination and does not warrant blocking this finding.
